history.period: Treta Yuga (legendary); no verifiable construction date
history.summary: Ramrekha Ghat on the Ganges at Buxar is a holy ghat (not a conventional temple building) associated with the Ramayana: one tradition says Rama bathed here after slaying the demoness Tadaka, fashioned a clay Shivling and worshipped it - Rama's hand-imprint and footprints are said to remain on the lingam and riverbank (the lingam is also called Rameshwarnath). Another account says Rama drew a line (rekha) with his arrow to mark the outlines of a yajna-shala after his coronation, giving the ghat its name; a third tradition says Rama, Lakshmana and Vishwamitra crossed the Ganga here en route to Janakpur. The traditions are legend, not documented history - flag the variants. It is a major Makar Sankranti bathing fair (Khichri fair, ~40,000-50,000 pilgrims per day over three days per one account). name: Ramrekha Ghat Temple
town_description: Buxar is an ancient town on the Ganges in western Bihar, known from the Ramayana as Siddhashram/Vedgarbhapuri and from modern history as the site of the 1764 Battle of Buxar. It is rich in Ramayana sites - Ramrekha Ghat, the Vishwamitra ashram area and the Ahalya sthan - and lies about 118-125 km from Patna and 130 km from Varanasi.

travel.road: Well connected by road to Patna and Varanasi; local autos/rickshaws within Buxar

visitor_information.best_time: September to April (Bihar tourism); Makar Sankranti (mid-January) for the Khichri fair
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open-access ghat; no fixed temple hours (verify) - Bihar tourism department office hours 9:30 AM-6 PM Mon-Fri are for the department, not the ghat
